description: Expected results for the official OpenHydroQual validation case 'first order decay in a batch reactor' (repo folder validation/first order decay in a batch reactor/, git 58933b3). One 1 m^3 reactor, constituent A starts at 2 g/m^3 and decays with k = 0.7 1/day for 5 days. inputs/ are the unmodified files from the upstream git tree. Run through the KI tools/run_ohq.py --fix-paths (rewrites only the three template-file paths, in a temp copy). Two clean runs gave byte-identical output.txt (deterministic).
engine_version: OpenHydroQual OHQLibTest + libOHQLib.so.2 built from ArashMassoudieh/OpenHydroQual git 58933b3 (2026-03-19), Qt 6.9

numeric_checks.name: max_rel_err_vs_exact
numeric_checks.why: OFFICIAL reference: model A concentration (linear interpolation of output) vs the official exact_solution.csv (C = 2 exp(-0.7 t), 51 points, t = 0..5) must stay within 5 % at every point. Upstream gives no number tolerance, only the plot OHQ_vs_Exact_Batch_first_order.pdf; 5 % is our bound. This run: 2.81 %.

numeric_checks.name: max_abs_err_vs_exact
numeric_checks.why: largest gap to the official exact solution (g/m^3), recorded from our run; the first-order implicit scheme (c_n_weight = 1) lags a little near t = 1, as the upstream plot also shows

numeric_checks.name: n_rows
numeric_checks.why: number of output time records (KI parse_output.py n_rows)

numeric_checks.name: t_final
numeric_checks.why: last output time (days); the solver steps a little past simulation_end_time = 5

numeric_checks.name: conc_first
numeric_checks.why: first written A concentration (start value is 2 g/m^3)

numeric_checks.name: conc_min
numeric_checks.why: lowest A concentration = final value (KI parse_output.py stats)

numeric_checks.name: conc_mean
numeric_checks.why: mean of A concentration over all records (KI parse_output.py stats)

numeric_checks.name: storage_min
numeric_checks.why: batch reactor: water volume stays 1 m^3 (no inflow, no outflow)

numeric_checks.name: storage_max
numeric_checks.why: batch reactor: water volume stays 1 m^3

numeric_checks.name: mass_minus_conc_x_storage_max
numeric_checks.why: mass check: A mass = concentration x volume at every record (gap only from 6-digit printing; this run 2e-05)

finished_check: return code 0 and the engine line 'Simulation finished!'
recorded_with: /home/server/knowledge-dissection-toolkit/auto_dissect/_work/OpenHydroQual/source/repo/OHQLibTest/OHQLibTest via the KI tools/run_ohq.py (--fix-paths, --resources <repo>/resources); output read with KI tools/parse_output.py and directly (interleaved t,value columns)
reference: inputs/exact_solution.csv (official, upstream git) and reference/OHQ_vs_Exact_Batch_first_order.pdf (official comparison plot)
notes: The .ohq file names its templates with the developer's Windows paths (C:/Program Files (x86)/..., E:/Projects/...). run_ohq.py --fix-paths writes first_order_decay_fixed.ohq in the temp dir with only those 3 lines changed to the local resources/ dir; nothing else in the file changes. The engine would also fall back to its default template dir by file name, so the result does not depend on this change.

The engine prints 'Failed to parse configuration ... Line 1, Column 1' and three 'has no property called inflow_concentration / A:inflow_concentration / inflow_timeseries' lines. They come from empty fields the old .ohq sets that the current templates renamed; this batch case has no inflow, so they do not change the result (checked against the exact solution).
